best_field_traits: SOUTHWESTERN / SCHEELE'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): a tall, commonly broad-leaved and hairy grass with a long, tapered, rather open bottlebrush-like head. Usually 1 (sometimes 2–3) LONG separate projecting bristles per spikelet, typically 10–35 mm in FNA/Kew. Unlike Reverchon's shorter sparse bristles, these long bristles are actually obvious in the saved flowering photograph. Edwards Plateau shady limestone canyon habitat is supportive, not conclusive.

Perennial tufted grass. CONFLICTING LOCAL DESCRIPTIONS of rootstock: Gibson's Williamson County flora records short underground whitish scaly rhizomes, while Hagenbuch & Lemke's 2015 Texas Hill Country vegetative treatment explicitly says rhizomes and stolons ABSENT. Do not treat underground spread as a stable identification character until a rooted, correctly determined specimen is documented.
Relatively broad, pubescent foliage with prominent midvein, often about 5–18 mm wide.
Conspicuous elongate single terminal bottlebrush-like flowering head; Texas A&M describes inflorescence about 15–35 cm long.
Spikelets generally about 2.1–2.6 mm in regional treatments, often associated with a single conspicuous long bristle.
Bristles are sterile reduced branchlets NOT a true awn of the floret; study both bristle and tiny spikelet.
Edwards Plateau limestone canyons/open woods and partially shaded areas are useful habitat cues, not proof of species or county nativity.

LIGULE WARNING: A Williamson County flora records a tiny truncate ciliate MEMBRANE, often <0.5 mm, while FNA/GrassBase describes a 1–2-mm hairy ligule. Open the blade/sheath junction and photograph both edge and hairs; white stem-node hairs are NOT a ligule.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole rooted perennial clump with broad hairy foliage and long tapering head, ruler
Macro of 1 (sometimes up to 3) bristles arising at individual spikelet base, 1-mm ruler
10–35 mm intact long bristle with attached 2.2–2.5 mm mature spikelet on same head
INSIDE blade/sheath junction at 10–20x, with 1-mm ruler: show membrane, short cilia and longer adjacent hairs separately; regional and broad flora reports vary
An entire excavated intact basal tuft and its attached roots, documenting whether genuine subterranean rhizomes are present or absent, paired to the same flowering specimen
crew_field_check: First find the WHOLE panicle and compare crowded/loose head arrangement without forcing species from silhouette.
Inspect an intact attached SPIKELET at 10–20×. Count the SUBTENDING PERSISTENT BRISTLES (sterile branches), not grass awns or protruding flower parts.
Record bristle count/length and spikelet length using a 1-mm scale, and compare the same-plant collar ligule.
Check a rooted base only where collecting is legal: annual fibrous millet vs knotty rhizomatous perennial parviflora/reverchonii, and perennial scheelei.
Existing archival images do not prove every underlying bristle count or rhizome; if unresolved identify Setaria sp.

At the base, the local floras conflict: Gibson documents rhizomes, Hagenbuch/Lemke (2015) explicitly say absent. Photograph an intact independently identified rooted plant before teaching the condition.
Show the inner ligule directly: regional Texas treatment finds an often <0.5-mm ciliate membrane, whereas FNA/GrassBase calls out a 1–2-mm hairy/fringed margin; node hairs are not ligule hairs.
next_photo_sequence_20261023: Verify existing three JPEGs display on the ordinary public species gallery; inspect actual image pixels before assigning anatomy markers.
Get rooted whole plant with head and foliage visible, not only one detached head.
Show entire attached inflorescence and several spikelet base close-ups.
Photograph the peeled-open INSIDE collar membrane plus ciliate edge and adjacent 1–2 mm hairs with 1-mm ruler, distinguishing them from external node/collar hairs.
Photograph attached mature spikelet plus persistent sterile-branchlet bristles and 1 mm scale; record species-appropriate numbers and measurements.
Finish with matched Setaria reverchonii, scheelei and parviflora comparative head/base photo, arrows only on clearly resolved structures.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Conspicuously projecting mostly solitary ~10–35 mm bristles on an elongate tapered head distinguish S. scheelei from sparse/shorter-bristled interrupted S. reverchonii and the many-bristled short rhizomatous S. parviflora. Annual foxtail millet S. italica can have a long head but usually denser/lobed cultivated seedheads, broad foliage and nonperennial roots. Check at least several mature spikelets; bristles are sterile branches, NOT awns.
not_reliable_alone: Color or texture of seedhead without bristle group macro
Bristles mistaken for true floret awns or flower stigmas
Mature spikelet counts read from a photo too small to show attachment
Cultivated or habitat context presented as confirmed local nativity

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: Look for a perennial tuft with broad often hairy blades and long TAPERING, relatively loose bottlebrush head. At a mature spikelet base find usually ONE conspicuous projecting bristle ~10–35 mm; that bristle is a sterile branchlet, NOT a floret awn.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_growth_and_collar: Perennial tufted grass with hairy nodes and blades 5–18 mm wide. Conflicting Hill Country sources: Gibson's Williamson County treatment has shallow nodally rooted scaly rhizomes; Hagenbuch & Lemke (2015) state rhizomes and stolons absent. Do not use presence/absence as a standalone ID until independently photographed. Leaf INNER ligule: short truncate membranous base ~0.5 mm with ciliate hairs 1–2 mm per Hill Country 2015, compare regional Gibson mostly <0.5 mm, and FNA/GrassBase 1–2-mm fringe descriptions.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_inflorescence_and_bristles: Long tapering open spike-like panicle ~15–25 cm in FNA/Kew, to ~35 cm in Texas A&M; usually 1, occasionally 2–3, persistent bristles per spikelet, ~10–35 mm, divergent. Spikelets ovate ~2.2–2.5 mm, with one sterile lower and one fertile upper floret.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_spikelet_glumes_lemmas_awns: Lower glume about half spikelet length, 3-veined; upper glume about 3/4 to near fertile-floret length, 5-veined. Lower sterile lemma near upper lemma length, 5-veined; lower palea present and about half upper palea length in FNA. Fertile upper lemma firm, finely cross-wrinkled, shortly pointed; no long true glume/lemma awns. Long conspicuous structures are persistent sterile-branch bristles.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: S. reverchonii has a slender interrupted head and sparse shorter bristles (~2–8 mm when present); S. parviflora has short dense heads, hard knotty rhizomes and many (4–12) shorter bristles per spikelet; cultivated S. italica is annual and often much denser. Edwards Plateau limestone canyon habitat supports but cannot certify identification.
last_mile_photo_holds: One rooted species-vetted perennial with hairy blade, collar and full tapering flowering head, cm scale.
Multiple 10–20× spikelets each showing attached one versus occasional 2–3 basal 10–35-mm bristles and a mm ruler; existing overview bristles are not a countable attachment voucher.
TRUE INNER ligule, peeled open with scale; document short membrane and cilia separately from 1–2 mm hairs described by FNA/Kew. Show hair-bearing culm node in distinct frame.
Dissected glumes, sterile lemma/palea and finely cross-wrinkled upper lemma with mm scale, plus matched S. reverchonii comparison.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.public_ready_criteria: Retain existing Kyla Miller CC BY-NC photo and NC restrictions, all arrows, taxonomy/nativity and source records. Keep FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until licensed verified attached anatomy/collar photos, exact arrow QA and rights-filtered public learner check.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.evidence_scope: Kew GrassBase and Flora of North America treatments plus Texas A&M regional habit description; no fine structures measured from existing image.

lane2_scheelei_basal_and_ligule_source_r.field_detection: HISTORICAL NOTE: Gibson describes rhizomes but Hagenbuch & Lemke (2015) says rhizomes absent; the older one-source phrasing was incomplete. See rootstock_conflict_20261027.
lane2_scheelei_basal_and_ligule_source_r.photo_protocol: Photograph entire independently identified flowering plant and full washed intact basal tuft. Record rhizomes if ACTUALLY visible; do not assume them, because local floras disagree. Open true INNER blade/sheath junction with mm scale showing ~0.5 mm ciliate membrane and ~1–2 mm cilia; photograph stem-node hairs separately.
lane2_scheelei_basal_and_ligule_source_r.leaf_ligule_interpretation: Two legitimate floristic treatments emphasize different aspects. Regional A. C. Gibson/Williamson County describes short, truncate MEMBRANOUS ligule with ciliate edge, mostly under 0.5 mm in the observed sample; Kew GrassBase/FNA broadly describes a 1–2-mm hispid or fringe-of-hairs ligule. Photograph both underlying membrane and hair fringe independently; do not make a 1–2-mm measured claim from external sheath/collar hairs.
lane2_scheelei_basal_and_ligule_source_r.separate_structures: The ring of hairs at a CULM NODE is not the blade/sheath INNER ligule; blade-edge hairs and the pilose collar also should not be labeled as ligule without inside view.

research: Gibson, A.C. Vascular Plants of Williamson County, Setaria scheelei (https://w3.biosci.utexas.edu/prc/K12/pdf/Setaria%20scheelei): shallow horizontal whitish rhizomes reported, to 3 mm, nodal roots.

Hagenbuch & Lemke 2015, Grasses of the Texas Hill Country, Phytoneuron 2015-4, pp. 61–62 (https://www.phytoneuron.net/2015Phytoneuron/04PhytoN-HillCountryGrasses.pdf): explicitly rhizomes and stolons ABSENT.
Hagenbuch & Lemke give ligule ~0.5 mm truncate membranous with 1–2 mm marginal hairs; distinguish membrane/hairs from stem node hairs.

items.label: Foxtail millet — dense, nodding cultivated seedheads
items.image_role: Real existing garden/crop overview showing branching millet head silhouette rather than microscopic identity
items.caption: Original credited overview shows multiple long densely packed, at times curved and drooping foxtail-millet heads with relatively wide leaves. It cannot expose individual basal bristle counts, ligules, exact millimeters or true annual root system.
items.why_it_matters: FOXTAIL MILLET (INTRODUCED annual crop/escape): start with stout annual culms, broad foliage, and a heavy dense often lobed or nodding foxtail head. Flora of North America usually describes 1–3 persistent subtending bristles (to ~12 mm), NOT 'numerous bristles beneath every spikelet'. A crop-derived head varies greatly; distinguish from perennial native bristlegrasses using rooted duration, panicle shape and ripe spikelets.
items.creator: Dinesh Valke
items.photo_status: Source labelled and locally archived real JPEG visually inspected 2026-10-21. Targets show only gross structures actually visible. Source identity provisional; bristle counts, microscopy and local nativity NOT independently proven.

items.caption: Original Stefan.lefnaer macro has green bract-like structures, a magenta protruding flowering tuft and photographer's 2-mm ruler. This view does NOT resolve 4–12 subtending bristles or the short knotty rhizome. Do not label magenta floral parts as sterile bristles.
items.why_it_matters: KNOTROOT BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): FIRST verify a living short hard knotty basal rhizome, then a generally short even-width dense foxtail head (~3–8 cm). FNA reports 4–12 persistent bristles, 2–12 mm long, beneath each spikelet; they must be counted from a genuinely intact head at 10–20×. Our only stored macro shows green bracts and pink emergent floral tissue with a 2-mm scale, NOT the perennial rhizome or a countable group of 4–12 basal bristles.

items.label: Reverchon's bristlegrass — interrupted slender panicle
items.image_role: Existing Texas source-labelled photo for sparse panicle architecture, not measured bristle anatomy
items.caption: Eric Knight's photo shows a narrow vertical seedhead with separated, sparse clusters of green spikelets. The finger is only an informal size cue. The tiny spikelet bases do not resolve the number or exact length of persistent bristles.
items.why_it_matters: REVERCHON'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): the existing real photo shows a skinny, often interrupted upright flowering head, with widely separated spikelet groupings. Its bristles are sparse—some spikelets appear almost unbristled—but FNA gives bristles about 2–8 mm where present; do NOT teach a hard ≤2 mm cutoff. Seek short knotty rhizomes, the stiff hair ligule (1–2 mm), and mature 2.1–4.5 mm spikelets. No bristle measurement is visible in the original picture.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Setaria — the bristle count is on a real spikelet
steps: START with the Kyla Miller archived photo: locate the long tapered flowering axis and conspicuous long outward projecting bristles. The three existing arrows mark visible gross structures, not counted spikelet attachments.

COMPARE THE EXTRA TWO ARCHIVED PHOTOS: the Gaiacoyote CC0 overview now has three pixel-checked arrows on the tapered flowering head, broad blade and clustered basal culms; these do NOT show roots, bristle attachments or the true ligule. Annika Lindqvist's CC BY image remains unannotated until actual bytes/pixels can be reviewed.

COUNT BRISTLES AT ONE ATTACHED RIPE SPIKELET under 10–20×: usually one, sometimes two or three distinct persistent sterile branch bristles; DO NOT confuse long bristles with true lemma awns. Literature lengths about 10–35 mm, not measured from the current photographs.

OPEN THE SAME SPIKELET against 1-mm scale: often 2.2–2.5 mm long; lower glume three-veined, upper glume five-veined; lower sterile lemma approximately five-veined; firm fertile upper lemma subtly cross-wrinkled. These microscopic parts are currently UNPHOTOGRAPHED.
UNFOLD the TRUE COLLAR on a mature leaf: measure 1–2-mm hair-fringe ligule separately from collar and sheath hairs. A broad hairy blade by itself cannot confirm the ligule.

MATCH ROOTED PERENNIAL BASE, broad often hairy leaves, and entire relatively loose tapered flowering head from the SAME individual. Compare S. reverchonii (often interrupted narrower head with sparse shorter bristles), S. parviflora (more numerous basal bristles, knotty rhizomes), and cultivated S. italica (dense annual head).

FIELD HOLD: retain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until a legally collected/photographed specimen gives real bristle insertion, attached fertile spikelet/glume details and a scaled ligule. Never aim new arrows at structures absent from the pixels.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: LONG conspicuous projecting mostly solitary bristles + relatively loose tapered foxtail panicle + hairy broad leaves; confirm the SINGLE bristle attachment and tiny hair-fringed ligule.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: 3 exact-source JPEGs are listed in the canonical species gallery. Gaiacoyote's 154,130-byte 800×592 CC0 overview was independently byte- and pixel-checked and has three gross-organ arrows; the separate Annika Lindqvist JPEG could not be byte-inspected in this run. No authenticated close-up proves bristle number per spikelet, glume veins, or 1–2-mm ligule. Existing CC BY-NC and all original source records preserved; source-page live license recheck for Gaiacoyote remains pending. PUBLIC RIGHTS NOTE 2026-10-25: CC BY-NC original is held from the public site; its 3 gross-organ arrows are preserved under visual_comparison.rights_held_comparison_items. Public same-species gallery now begins with 2 already archived CC0/CC BY originals; true measured anatomy remains missing.

what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole rooted perennial clump with broad hairy foliage and long tapering head, ruler
Macro of 1 (sometimes up to 3) bristles arising at individual spikelet base, 1-mm ruler
10–35 mm intact long bristle with attached 2.2–2.5 mm mature spikelet on same head
Leaf collar ligule 1–2 mm and broad pubescent blade with true width scale
Intact excavated rooted basal tuft with all adjacent lower shoots and full attached flowering stem; identify if genuine rhizome is present OR absent

field_id_references.use: Verified regional botanical morphology and distinctions; no photo license implied

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LONG TAPERED BRISTLEGRASS HEAD
field_id_short_tiles.short: LOOK HERE FIRST: tall perennial with broad often hairy leaves and loose tapering bottlebrush
field_id_short_tiles.details: A coarse perennial with culms ~60–120 cm and often 5–18 mm broad blades. Flowering head roughly 15–25 cm in FNA/Kew, up to ~35 cm in Texas A&M. Existing image indices 0–1 show public-reusable broad architecture; original CC BY-NC image is held outside the public gallery and retains its existing rights hold.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ACTUAL HEAD PHOTO — SAME-PLANT ROOTED HABIT NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · SHORT HAIR-FRINGE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Open the inner collar: distinguish a minute ciliate membrane from adjacent longer hairs
field_id_short_tiles.details: Williamson County treatment describes a tiny truncate ciliate membrane, often <0.5 mm; FNA/GrassBase describes a roughly 1–2 mm hairy/fringed ligule. These may emphasize different portions of the collar. Expose the inner blade/sheath junction with 1-mm scale, document membrane and hairs separately, and never substitute hairy stem nodes for a ligule. Existing photographs do not prove the exact dimensions.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · MOSTLY ONE LONG BASAL BRISTLE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Usually 1 (sometimes 2–3) persistent bristles per spikelet, about 10–35 mm
field_id_short_tiles.details: Long projecting structures are sterile branchlets, NOT floret lemma awns. Several bristles are obvious in gross flowering photos, but actual number and insertion at one ~2.2–2.5 mm spikelet are unresolved. Photograph multiple attached ripe units at 10–20× with ruler; do not infer a universal count from a distant head.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · TINY 2.2–2.5 MM SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Inspect one ripe spikelet beside 1-mm scale, not a long bristle mistaken for the floret
field_id_short_tiles.details: Regional treatment reports mature spikelets ~2.2–2.5 mm. Lower glume roughly half spikelet length, 3-veined; upper glume roughly 3/4 to near fertile lemma length, 5-veined. These are treatment-relative proportions, not direct measurements from the archived head photos.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · FIRM FINELY WRINKLED UPPER LEMMA
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma ~fertile lemma length; upper fertile lemma hard, cross-wrinkled and unawned
field_id_short_tiles.details: Lower sterile lemma commonly 5-veined; a shorter lower palea may be present. Firm upper fertile lemma has fine transverse wrinkles, without a long true lemma awn. To demonstrate this, photograph a mature ~2.2–2.5 mm spikelet opened to show lower/upper glumes, sterile lemma/palea and fertile lemma.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · CHECK REVERCHON AND KNOTROOT
field_id_short_tiles.short: Mostly solitary 10–35 mm bristles versus sparse short S. reverchonii and many-bristled S. parviflora
field_id_short_tiles.details: S. reverchonii has a narrower often interrupted head and sparse ~2–8 mm bristles where present; S. parviflora generally 4–12 bristles per spikelet and knotty rhizomes; S. italica is a dense-headed annual. Limestone canyon habitat is supportive only, never proof of taxon or Hays native status. Compare measured ripe attachments and the true collar.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD COMPARISON — MATCHED REPRODUCTIVE MACROS NEEDED

NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: Species-vouchered rooted perennial with broad hairy blades, true collar and whole 15–35 cm tapering panicle, cm scale.
At least three ripe 2.2–2.5 mm spikelets each showing 1 (sometimes 2–3) attached 10–35 mm basal bristles with 1-mm bar; verify individual insertion.

Opened blade/sheath junction with 1-mm ruler, documenting both the tiny truncate ciliate membranous ligule (often <0.5 mm in Williamson County flora) and adjacent 1–2 mm hairs described in broader treatments; do not infer membrane length from hair length.
Dissected mature lower/upper glumes, sterile lemma/palea and hard cross-wrinkled fertile lemma; matched S. reverchonii and S. parviflora reproductive units.
